This feels like an Adult Swim short (derogatory). Rango has an instantly compelling premise, but too bad its execution is everything I do not want from a premise as delightfully absurd as a hero's journey from cowardly Lizard to Clint Eastwood. It's so painfully self aware and satirical of everything that it just loses the magic that it could have had. Rango is much more of a comedy than an adventure, a Western or a drama, and it sucks that this is the approach they went for. You are absolutely not supposed to watch Once Upon A Time In The West before this, because most of the elements in this film that make you go "oh shit, that's actually really cool" is just stripped from that one. I don't even like Leone or that movie that much for the matter, but I genuinely checked out once the literal main theme song is just a lackluster spoof of Man With A Harmonica. So many shots are just ripped from Leone without even any interesting remixing of ideas like what Tarantino usually does, just homage for the sake of homage. The movie itself also does not hold up on its own. Rango is supposed to be flawed, but he's so fucking irritatingly incompetent and genuinely idiotic that it makes me completely unable to root for his character. He's not a likeable loser or a charming asshole, he's just that one annoying kid in school that you lowkey understand why they're bullied. And all the characters are just whatever, Beans is the only character that I actually find kinda sweet, too bad she's just the damsel in distress. The movie also feels really really long. Could have ended like 15 minutes before if we got rid of all the shitty Leone homages and trimmed one unnecessary set piece. The animation is pretty gorgeous though, that I can't lie. It's too bad so much of it has to be a homage of Leone that it lacks originality. That (SPOILER) character appearing to Rango before the final act is a little tacky, but it's pretty cute. Puts a smile on my face.

c’est pour les bewbew. j’ai pas ris à un seul moment. l’humour est désastreux. mais ce qui l’est encore plus c’est le script. tout est verbalisé, ça parle à tout bout de champ. je regarde un film ou j’écoute un podcast ? j’arrive pas à savoir là malgré ça, j’ai apprécie l’univers western. tous les codes hollywoodiens sont présents. j’ai eu l’impression que petit à petit rango s’imprègne la personnalité et le comportement de john wayne pour recréer l’homme viril hégémonique et la suprématie blanche américaine. il m’a semblé qu’il y avait aussi une référence aux huit salopards de tarantino quand le protagoniste rencontre le soi-disant « chercheur » dans une zone enneigée en pleine tempête. (ou alors c’était une référence à the searchers ?) la prévention écologique est plutôt intéressante. elle met en garde sur le fait que les activités anthropiques tuent des espèces animales. l’unique acteur de l’épuisement de l’eau est l’humain. j’aurai cependant aimé que le film aille au-delà de l’aspect empathique envers les animaux, pour qu’il avertisse que l’humain se condamne lui-même. une extinction partielle/totale de la faune et de la flore aboutie inéluctablement à la mort de l’espèce humaine. ça aurait été possible en plus d’intégrer 2-3 plans pour montrer cette implication au moment où rango découvre la métropole

I remember really wanting to see this when it released (though in my memory it released way earlier than it did in reality). I remember so many people singing its praises. I saved Rango for a long time, as I have with a lot of these more mainstream-but-beloved movies. As is often the case, it really has nothing going for it without nostalgia backing it up. Often looking really good, Rango opens pretty strong with a string of whacky cartoon slapstick setpieces, then it completely runs out of steam when it drops into the most generic American family, action/comedy movie template story and just plods through it with nothing memorable, no real characters, no real personality. The character designs are fun. I ended up having to pause it and return 24 hours later because it was boring me to death. I don't think a family comedy should be capable of being boring, but it's so completely lacking in an identity of it's own that there's nothing to connect to. The acid-western epiphany sequence towards the end shakes some energy into the film, by presenting the act of walking into traffic as the solution to all of your problems in a film primarily for children... And of course the epiphany is that capitalism and greed are wasting resources and destroying the earth, which is never really engaged with at all and then Rango wastes loads of water and causes massive amounts of damage and is basically bailed out by everyone else, as he is for the entire story, leaving there with pretty much nothing of value by the end. I guess the Johnny Depp mania of the era was hard carrying this thing.

This is undeniably very unique and clever, with a cool visual style. It just isn’t my favorite on a personal level. I’ve never really seen a true western, which might be part of the problem, so the parody doesn’t fully land. The sense of humor feels a little off, the plot dragged quite a bit, and I don’t really like any of the characters. It’s not a bad movie by any means, just not for me.

Bumbling, pointless plot driven by pseudo-epiphanies and writers room anterograde amnesia. The husks of a bunch of better movies (True Grit, Chinatown, etc.) duct-taped together. Its very best jokes would've only barely made the cut on an average episode of The Animaniacs. Feel a kind of pity now for the gay porn star with the huge Rango shoulder tat. The animation goes crazy for 2011 though, even if it's strange that they'd go to such lengths making everyone look like villagers from a rated-E version of Resident Evil 4.

Hmm muistin että tää olis ollu parempi... ei siis täysin huono mutta paljon asioita joista en pitänyt. Sekava, poukkoileva ja mitäänsanomaton tarina, unohdettavat hahmot ja todella, TODELLA pakotettua huumoria etenkin ensimmäisellä puoliskolla. Siis oikeasti, tuntui että yhden yhtä asiaa ei oteta leffan ekalla puolikkaalla tosissaan ja joka ikinen lause tuplataan jollain vitsillä, gagilla tai hassuttelulla. Ihan saatanan raivostuttavaa. Lisäksi tuo Rango hahmona on niin perseestä todella pitkään, että kun loppupuolella vihdoin jotain kauan odotettua hahmokehitystä tapahtuu, ei se ilmene mitenkään uskottavana. Onneksi jälkipuoli leffasta on ylipäätään parempi ja vakavampi sävyltään. Olisi ollut sitä alusta asti ja huumoria siroteltuna sinne tänne, niin tässä olisi ollut potentiaalia. Tuntui nyt siltä, että ne vaan tyhjensi jonkun kuratoimattoman vitsivihkosensa vaan sarjatulella, ja sitten muisti että ainiin tässä pitää joku juonikin tehdä ja ohoh meillähän olis tässä ihan hyviäkin aineksia joita vois käyttää. Sinänsä harmi, koska animaatiotyyli on hyvin ainutlaatuinen ja mieleenpainuva, ja moni visuaalinen ja esteettinen ratkaisu on todella osuvia. Ja OSA huumorista on oikein hauskaakin, tai olisi hauskaa jos sille antaisi tilaa vaikuttaa. Sinänsä idea tämmöisestä "aikuisten" animaatiosta, jossa on paljon kaksimielisiä vitsejä ja sivistyssanoja, ja melkoisen rujo animaatiotyyli, on todela hyvä ja toimisi, jos siihen uskallettaisiin nojata sellaisenaan. Nyt tämä tuntuu pokkuroinnilta lasten hömppäelokuvan ja vakavasti otettavan aikuisten leffan välillä, eikä tee kumpaakaan hääppöisesti.

The main attraction is the charisma and likability of the titular Rango, along with the interesting surrealist elements and designs. Apart from that, it doesn’t have a lot going for it. Character work is pretty minimal, and the plot is so generic and predictable that it feels like a waste of time to finish the film. There’s clearly a lot of creativity and passion behind the fine details of the movie, so it’s a shame the ball was dropped for the fundamentals.
